The AI Factory in 3D: Fly Around a 100 MW Campus

A three-dimensional, animated model of a reference AI factory campus of about 100 megawatts on roughly 100 acres. Drag to move around like a map, right-drag or use two fingers to rotate and tilt, scroll or pinch to zoom, and watch power, coolant and data flow between the substation, generators, batteries, two liquid-cooled data halls, dry coolers, network core and storage. Switch the overlay between the hardware in each building and the software that runs on it, take the roof off a hall to see its rack rows, and then scale the land up from 1 megawatt to a terawatt.

Open the model ↓ Land at every scale ↓
⚠️ A reference design, not a real site. Layout, dimensions and counts are our illustration of a typical liquid-cooled AI campus, assembled from the site's case studies (Colossus, Stargate Abilene, Fairwater, Rainier, Hyperion) and explainers. Technology names are examples of what is commonly used, not a claim about any one operator. Land figures are our model, anchored to two reported campuses. Disclosure: Claude, made by Anthropic, helps write this site.

2. Component guide

Every part of the model, with the hardware usually found there and the software that runs it. Tap a row to fly to it.

3. Land at every scale: 1 MW to 1 TW

How much land does an AI factory need? Pick a size. The squares are drawn to true relative scale; the view zooms out by a factor of ten every few steps. Campus land only by default; add the solar farm and batteries it would take to run the campus around the clock from sunshine alone.

4. Scale table

Our model. Campus density: about 1 acre per MW below 1 GW and 0.8 acre per MW above it (Compact ×0.6, Spacious ×1.6). Anchors: Amazon's Project Rainier, ~1,200 acres for ~2.2 GW of reported grid draw (~0.55 acre/MW); Meta's Hyperion, ~4,000 acres for a planned 5 GW (~0.8 acre/MW). Solar: ~4.5 MW of panels per MW of round-the-clock load at ~6 acres per MW of panels, plus batteries (our assumption; NREL reports 5–10 acres per MW for utility-scale PV). GPUs: ~450 per MW of facility power (NVL72-class rack ~120–140 kW for 72 GPUs, plus cooling overhead). Energy assumes full load all year.

5. How we built it

The model is drawn with a small custom 3D renderer on an HTML canvas, with no libraries: every building is a set of shaded faces sorted by distance each frame. The plot is 760 × 560 m (about 105 acres). The two data halls are 200 × 70 m each, with electrical galleries along both long walls and about 400 rack positions per hall in the roof-off view, roughly 50 MW of liquid-cooled racks each. Dry coolers sit in yards beside each hall in a closed loop; batteries and on-site generation share a bus with the grid feed. Counts are rounded for clarity.

Related maps: the AI factory cut open (floors and bottlenecks), the AI factory from above (2D site plan with articles), AI Factories at a Glance (real campuses) and the Stack Innovation Map.

Sources for the land anchors: our case studies Project Rainier and Meta Prometheus & Hyperion; NREL: Land-Use Requirements for Solar Power Plants in the United States (2013). Electricity comparisons: US generation ≈4,200 TWh and world ≈30,000 TWh per year (2023, rounded).
